newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Rivlin calls U.S. economy "highly positive".
newsitem.headline: Fed's Rivlin calls U.S. economy "highly positive".

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin on Tuesday gave high marks to the U.S. economy, but said it was unclear how much of that could be credited to monetary policy.
"The performance of the economy ... right now is highly positive," she said. "But it is not clear how much of the economic progress can be attributed to monetary policy."
Rivlin made the remarks in prepared testimony to the House Banking Committee on the central bank's overall strategic plan.
The Fed policymaker said the central bank conducts monetary policy with the aim of achieving maximum sustainable economic growth. "Price stability fosters that goal," she added.

The Fed also seeks to promote a safe, sound and competitive banking system and stable financial markets through regulation, supervision and by acting as a lender of last resort in financial emergencies, she said.
Rivlin defended the regional structure of the Fed, describing it as one of the central bank's great strengths.
"The challenge confronting strategic planning at the Federal Reserve is to find a balance between decentralized regional planning ... and the need for a more comprehensive national plan," she said.
